To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the social context of exercise is important for understanding and promoting exercise adherence.
exercise adherence can be fostered by creating social identities within groups that are consistent with the exercise goals and that these identities can be formed by the exercise leaders.

(1) social identity formation is a powerful determinant of exercise program adherence; (2) the formation of social identity is a function of the extent of group homogeneity and the extent of group distinctiveness; (3) social identities are formed within the context of the group; and (4) social identities are a product of the interaction of the individual and the group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of social groups and social identity in the promotion of exercise adherence.
how people form group identities, the consequences of these identities, and how group identities can be used to foster positive health outcomes.
the role of social identity in exercise adherence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social identity model of behaviour change is a useful theoretical framework to consider when developing interventions that aim to promote exercise adherence.
exercise adherence can be fostered through intervention by considering how group membership influences social identification.
the self categorization theory can be used to explain how social identity is formed and how this can be used as a basis for promoting exercise adherence through groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand how people form social identities within groups.
social identities are formed within groups and that the formation of these social identities can be used to increase exercise adherence.
we found that group-based exercise adherence interventions can be effective, and that they are effective in part through social identity processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social identities are a key determinant in exercise adherence.

group exercise programs should be designed with a view towards the development of social identities that are relevant and meaningful to participants, and that the social context of group exercise is an important determinant of adherence to exercise programs.
